input: expression is a valid expression of length 1 through 20000 in the grammar E := t | f | !(E) | &(E[,E]...) | |(E[,E]...). NOT has exactly one operand; AND and OR each have at least one operand. There is no whitespace or other syntax. Collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse/accessor-backed collections. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. Every collection length and computed allocation size fits [0,4294967295], with padded sizes explicitly included. No concurrent mutation or built-in monkey-patching is allowed. Preconditions are not runtime-checked, and allocation/resource capacity or completion is not guaranteed by declared bounds. JavaScript integer inputs are primitive safe-integer Number, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt.
return: A Python bool / JavaScript boolean giving the value of the full expression.
mutation_aliasing: Inputs and caller-held aliases remain unchanged; working state is private. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: Only stack indices bounded by expression length and boolean flags are used. On a closing parenthesis, every immediate operand has already reduced to t or f, while the matching operator remains directly below the opening parenthesis. Validity and operand-count rules are preconditions, not parser validation behavior. All integer inputs/intermediates remain within [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991]; no bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: For expression length n: O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary stack storage. Every token or reduced value is pushed and popped at most once. There is no recursive call-stack dependency, including at maximum nesting depth. Bounds include ordinary built-in operations/allocations and assume bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time indexing, amortized append/pop and any explicitly stated hash/sort behavior.
source_accounting: The complete standalone source is 825 UTF-8 bytes, including every helper, Solution wrapper, signature, loop, built-in call, annotation/comment, whitespace and terminal newline. Helpers are fully charged per candidate, not free shared libraries. No imports, runtime-generated implementations or hidden source expansion are used. Any eventual judge-interface adapter is additional charged source.
